title: Agents as bounded state machines
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects agents as bounded state machines with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Evaluate final goal completion and trajectory safety separately.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: An agent repeatedly selects actions based on observations and state. A deterministic workflow has transitions specified by the application; an agentic transition delegates some choice to a model. Use deterministic steps when inputs and required operations are known, and agentic selection when investigation requires choosing evidence paths.

State is the current task record, including goal, evidence, steps, budget and status. Memory is persisted information across steps or sessions; it needs scope and retention rules. A chat transcript alone is a poor substitute for explicit typed state.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Represent the loop with observe, decide, validate, authorize, execute and terminate stages. Each transition consumes a step and checks remaining wall-time and token budgets. Stop on goal completion, insufficient evidence, repeated action signatures or exhausted budget.

The automation assistant reads a failure, retrieves similar history and prepares a draft recommendation. Application code enforces allowed tools and approval, even when the model selects the next action. Persist a trace so a failed run can be replayed without repeating writes.
sections.code:
seen=set();budget=4
for action in ['read:F1','search:timeout','search:timeout']:
    if action in seen or budget<=0: break
    seen.add(action);budget-=1

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: An agent loops over the same unsuccessful search because its state lacks a record of tried queries. Another declares success after proposing a patch without checking the requested goal. These are state/termination failures, not merely bad wording.
Test repeated signatures, failed tools, missing observations, cancelled tasks and deadline expiry. Recovery may choose another permitted read, but it must not expand privileges or reset its budget.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Evaluate final goal completion and trajectory safety separately. Count unnecessary calls, denied calls, repeated actions, cost and elapsed time. A short correct trace is often better than an elaborate chain.

For SDETs, state machines provide inspectable contracts: every action has a predecessor state, authorization outcome and effect. Replay traces against deterministic fixture tools before enabling a live decision model.

mistake: An agent loops over the same unsuccessful search because its state lacks a record of tried queries. Another declares success after proposing a patch without checking the requested goal. These are state/termination failures, not merely bad wording.
takeaway: Evaluate final goal completion and trajectory safety separately.

exercise.prompt: Implement the function in the editor. def stop_reason(actions,steps,limit,done):. Use the worked contract, handle the stated boundary cases, and inspect the behavior checks.
exercise.solution:
def stop_reason(actions,steps,limit,done):
    if done:return 'complete'
    if steps>=limit:return 'budget'
    if len(actions)!=len(set(actions)):return 'loop'
    return 'continue'

quiz.question: A candidate for agents as bounded state machines meets the happy path but fails the phase's documented counterexample. What is the defensible decision?
options: Hold release, preserve the failing case and fix the responsible boundary
Release because the happy path passed
Delete the failing case to improve the score
quiz.explanation: The failing counterexample disproves the claimed contract. Retain it as regression evidence and rerun the corrected boundary.
